prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B048 first, but that agreement is not the argument. The argument is the unbroken chain from hormone physiology to medicine: the incretin effect, proglucagon processing, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, its insulinotropic, satiety and gastric actions, then drugs validated in large independent outcome trials with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high, and the mechanism is stable after decades of replication. Drucker, Holst and Mojsov are the most defensible basic-science trio under the three-person cap. I would keep this as a single-achievement prize rather than dilute it with a second part, because the second candidates (B050, B031) each carry a larger attribution problem than B048 does.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is attribution. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested and the supplied list omits Habener and others. Excluding Lotte Bjerre Knudsen means the prize honours the physiology and not the engineering of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide), which is where most patient benefit arises, so a critic can say we reward the idea and skip the drug. Counting only three of four credited names also forces a judgement call between discovery and development that the evidence does not settle.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B005 (imatinib) second and treats Knudsen's industrial role as a possible alternative to Mojsov within B048.
responses.response: I disagree on swapping Knudsen for Mojsov. Identification of the active form is an enabling discovery on which the analogue engineering depends, and replacing it would turn a physiology prize into a pharmaceutical one. On B005 I rank it lower than you: the story is complete and mature, and the BCR-ABL upstream credit (Rowley, Nowell, and the fusion kinase work) is outside the credited names, which makes a Druker-Lydon-Sawyers prize look unfairly truncated. It is a fair alternative, but I would not place it above B050 or B031.

responses.point: Perlmann places B031 (CAR-T) second and B017 (UPR) third, but puts B050 (optogenetics) only sixth as principally a research tool.
responses.response: I take the tool-versus-discovery point seriously, and it is the main weakness of B050. But I think it is too severe. Optogenetics is a conceptual change in what neuroscience can establish causally, and it has served the same function that Nobel-recognised methods have served before. Where I agree with you is that B050 cannot be a clean three-person prize: six names for three slots is a real defect. That is why I keep B031 close to it as an alternative, and why I read your support for B017 as a coherent, compact two-person case that I would weigh more heavily than I did in my own ballot.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks TNF blockade (B001) second and sees cGAS-STING (B044) as relevant to autoimmunity, while noting Eshhar's absence weakens B031.
responses.response: I share your Eshhar concern for B031, and it is why I would not make CAR-T my preferred second part. On B001, the Feldmann-Maini pairing is clean, but the field has been mature for a long time and the credit for TNF cloning and antibody engineering lies outside the list. I see it as a strong, safe candidate for a later year, not a reason to change the configuration now. I am less persuaded than you on B044 because therapeutic translation of cGAS-STING has not yet been delivered.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B050 second and B016 (TOR) fourth, and flags that the three-person limit forces out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck.
responses.response: We agree that B050 is the main runner-up and that the exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck is a real weakness. I would push on this further than you do: if the committee cannot defend a three-name selection there, B050 should wait rather than be awarded with a contestable list. On B016 I am less enthusiastic than you are because Hall's origin claim is clear but allocation to Schreiber and Sabatini is genuinely arguable.

uncertainties: Priority for identification of active GLP-1 (Mojsov versus Habener and others) is not resolved by the supplied material.
Whether the committee should credit physiology alone or include industrial analogue development (Knudsen) within the three-person cap.
Whether any second achievement is worth adding given attribution gaps in B050 and B031.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B048. I note a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, which does not involve any shortlisted candidate. B050 (optogenetics) is a method I and colleagues in my field use, but I have no documented personal tie to its candidates.
